questions.question: Which of the following is the correct way to start an if-statement in Python?

Consider the following code block:

```
x = 5
if x > 4:
    print('x is greater than 4')
```

What is the output?
Which of the following will cause a syntax error in an if-statement?

Given the following code, what will be the output?

```
x = 10
if x == 5:
    print('x is 5')
else:
    print('x is not 5')
```

What will be the output of the following code?

```
x = 5
y = 10
if x > y:
    print('x is greater than y')
elif x < y:
    print('x is less than y')
else:
    print('x is equal to y')
```
Which block of code correctly uses the 'elif' statement?

options.A:

else if x < 5: pass
options.B:
if x > 5: pass
elif x < 5: pass
else: pass
options.C:
if x > 5 then pass
elif x < 5 then pass
options.D:
if x > 5: pass
elif: x < 5: pass
else: pass
